image.alt: the Nairobi skyline seen across Nairobi National Park, Kenya

places.text: The only capital on earth with a national park inside the city limits, and lions in sight of the skyline.
places.title: Nairobi, Green City in the Sun

image.alt: an ornately carved Swahili door in a coral stone wall in Lamu, Kenya

places.text: Swahili coral-rag houses with inner courtyards, and doors carved in Lamu and shipped up the coast.
places.title: Coral Stone and Carved Doors

image.alt: elephants crossing the plain at Amboseli beneath Kilimanjaro, Kenya

places.text: The Big Five, plus the reticulated giraffe and Grevy's zebra that live nowhere south of here.
places.title: Wildlife on the Savannah

image.alt: wildebeest crossing the Mara river during the great migration, Kenya

places.text: Between July and October a million wildebeest cross the Mara river, and the crocodiles are already waiting.
places.title: The Great Migration

image.alt: Thomson's Falls dropping into the fern gorge at Nyahururu, Kenya

places.text: The Ewaso Ng'iro drops seventy-four metres into a fern gorge at Nyahururu, on the way north to Samburu.
places.title: Thomson's Falls

image.alt: flamingos massed on the shallows of Lake Nakuru, Kenya

places.text: Nakuru, Bogoria and Elementaita hold soda water, hot springs and flamingo in numbers that change by the season.
places.title: Flamingo Country

image.alt: white sand and dhows on Diani Beach on the Indian Ocean, Kenya

places.text: Diani, Watamu and Lamu: white sand, warm Indian Ocean, and a coastline that traded with Arabia for a thousand years.
places.title: The Swahili Coast

image.alt: Maasai elders in red shuka cloth on the open plains, Kenya

places.text: Two Kenyas: the cattle-keeping highlands and the coral-stone, Arabic-inflected coast.
places.title: Maasai and Swahili

image.alt: a Samburu warrior with beaded ornaments in the northern drylands, Kenya

places.text: Samburu in the northern drylands, Maasai in the south, both still moving cattle between seasonal grazing.
places.title: Samburu and Maasai

image.alt: dhow racing during the Lamu cultural festival, Kenya

places.text: Dhow races, donkey races, henna and taarab music in the alleys of a town with almost no cars.
places.title: Lamu Cultural Festival

image.alt: Maasai women stringing beadwork ornaments, Kenya

places.text: Maasai beadwork, Kisii soapstone carving, and kiondo sisal baskets made the way they always were.
places.title: Beadwork and Kisii Stone

image.alt: brightly painted matatu minibuses in a Nairobi street, Kenya

places.text: Painted, over-amplified matatus, Maasai Market on rotation through the week, and tea at every stop.
places.title: Matatus and Markets

image.alt: the Great Rift Valley escarpment and floor seen from the Naivasha road, Kenya

places.text: The escarpment drops away below the Naivasha road, holding a chain of soda lakes and dormant volcanoes.
places.title: The Great Rift Valley

image.alt: the jagged glaciated peaks of Mount Kenya above the moorland

places.text: Equatorial glaciers, giant lobelia, and a trekking route to Point Lenana that needs no technical climbing.
places.title: Mount Kenya, 5,199 m

image.alt: dense canopy and hanging vines inside Kakamega Forest, Kenya

places.text: The only Kenyan remnant of the Guineo-Congolian rainforest that once ran clear across the continent.
places.title: Kakamega, the Last of It

image.alt: a hot-air balloon over the Maasai Mara plains at sunrise, Kenya

places.text: Up before dawn, an hour over the plains at treetop height, and breakfast on the grass where you land.
places.title: Balloon Over the Mara

image.alt: nyama choma roasting over charcoal at a Nairobi grill, Kenya

places.text: Goat roasted over charcoal, maize meal, sukuma wiki, and coastal biryani that came in by dhow.
places.title: Nyama Choma and Ugali

image.alt: the coral ramparts of Fort Jesus above Mombasa old harbour, Kenya

places.text: Portuguese, built 1593, taken and retaken nine times — now UNESCO World Heritage above the old harbour.
places.title: Fort Jesus, Mombasa

image.alt: carved wooden doors and coral stone alleys in Lamu Old Town, Kenya

places.text: The oldest continuously inhabited Swahili settlement, carved doors, coral rag walls and no room for a car.
places.title: Lamu Old Town

image.alt: a community conservancy ranger team on patrol near the Maasai Mara, Kenya

places.text: Community conservancies lease grazing land back for wildlife, and the lease pays the schools around the Mara.
places.title: The Conservancies

image.alt: cyclists on the track between the cliffs of Hell's Gate National Park, Kenya

places.text: The one Kenyan park you can walk and cycle through, with gorge scrambling and geothermal steam.
places.title: Walking Hell's Gate

image.alt: a luxury tented safari camp overlooking the Maasai Mara plains, Kenya

places.text: Small tented camps on private conservancies, night drives and off-road access the main reserve does not allow.
places.title: Camps on the Mara

image.alt: black rhino grazing on the Ol Pejeta conservancy at dawn, Kenya

places.text: Ol Pejeta and Lewa run some of Africa's most closely monitored rhino populations, funded by the beds on the property.
places.title: Rhino, Counted Daily

image.alt: elephants beneath Mount Kilimanjaro seen from Amboseli at sunrise, Kenya

places.text: The mountain is in Tanzania; the view of it is in Kenya, and it is only clear for an hour at each end of the day.
places.title: Kilimanjaro from Amboseli

image.alt: the salt pan and dunes of the Chalbi desert in northern Kenya

places.text: The desert north: Chalbi's salt pan, Marsabit's forested crater and the road down to Lake Turkana.
places.title: Chalbi and Marsabit

image.alt: acacia silhouetted against a red sunset on the Kenyan savannah

places.text: Migration, glacier, reef and desert inside one border, with the infrastructure to see all four in a fortnight.
places.title: Magical Kenya
